items.text: Maxine Waters is the U.S. Representative for California’s 43rd District, a seat she has held since 1991. She is the ranking member of the House Financial Services Committee and chaired the panel from 2019 to 2023. Before her election to Congress, Waters served 14 years in the California State Assembly and was the Democratic Caucus Chair. She worked as a teacher and Head Start volunteer coordinator, and she founded the youth job-training group Project Build and co-founded the nonprofit Black Women’s Forum.

sentences.text: Maxine Waters is the U.S. Representative for California’s 43rd District, a seat she has held since 1991.
She is the ranking member of the House Financial Services Committee and chaired the panel from 2019 to 2023.
Before her election to Congress, Waters served 14 years in the California State Assembly and was the Democratic Caucus Chair.
She worked as a teacher and Head Start volunteer coordinator, and she founded the youth job-training group Project Build and co-founded the nonprofit Black Women’s Forum.

items.text: In 2026 Waters spoke out against the Trump administration’s attempt to suspend federal homelessness grants for Los Angeles, which a court order blocked, protecting approximately $241 million in funding that supports programs for more than 11,000 people. She says she introduced the Ending Homelessness Act and worked across the aisle on the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which was signed into law. She voted in favor of a resolution to direct the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in Iran and against attempts to override California harbor-craft pollution rules. She says she helped direct federal resources to the Jordan Downs public-housing revitalization in Watts, where 863 new apartments have been completed. Her official website says she spearheaded the Minority AIDS Initiative in 1998, and that under her leadership its annual funding rose from $156 million to about $400 million.
